sentence: TileLang's own fallback to it "runs 1.81× slower", so an sm_80 build is possible-but-slow rather than impossible
problem: The note's 1.81× is measured on H800 SXM (Hopper) where the PV GEMM falls back to `mma.sync` because V is not K-major — a layout-induced fallback inside an SM90 kernel, not an sm_80/Ampere measurement. The note never mentions sm_80, Ampere, or an sm_80 build, so the inference 'an sm_80 build is possible-but-slow rather than impossible' is the report's own extrapolation.
suggested_fix: Soften to what the note supports: 'TileLang's own `mma.sync` fallback path runs 1.81× slower on H800 SXM, so an sm_80 build would be slower still — the note contains no sm_80 measurement.'

sentence: and the indexer's cost is additive and measured at 3.5× the kernel it feeds
problem: dsa_referencepy supports the mechanism (top-k non-differentiable; indexer trained by a clipped-log KL gradient against main-attention scores, not end-to-end) but contains no 3.5× figure and no additive-cost measurement. The 3.5× ratio is in published-as-a-conference-paper-at-colm-2026 ('the indexer is ~3.5x the sparse-attention cost', 5.6 ms vs 1.6 ms at 64K on A100).
suggested_fix: Add [[published-as-a-conference-paper-at-colm-2026]] after '3.5× the kernel it feeds' (or move [[dsa_referencepy]] to cover only the distillation clause).

sentence: trailing LM loss at 32K is 1.546 against 1.464 for full attention
problem: The GitHub note supports only the `flash-attn==2.6.3` pin and contains none of the loss figures. The 1.546/1.464 numbers are bound to [[moba-mixture-of-block-attention-for]], where they are the multiplicative coefficients of fitted scaling-law curves (1.546·C^-0.108 vs 1.464·C^-0.097), not trailing LM-loss values at 32K; the qualitative claim (MoBA marginally worse at 32K in all five runs) is supported, but the numbers are quoted in the wrong unit/context.
suggested_fix: Keep the GitHub citation for the pin; rewrite the loss clause as 'MoBA's fitted 32K trailing-loss curve sits above full attention's in all five runs (1.546·C^-0.108 vs 1.464·C^-0.097)' and cite [[moba-mixture-of-block-attention-for]] there.

sentence: published architecture effects are 0.014–0.082 nats against a 3.5%-relative single-run floor
problem: The MoBA note contains none of 0.014, 0.082, 'nats', or a 3.5% floor; its only effect-size numbers are the fitted coefficients 1.546/1.464. The 0.0139-nat figure is in conditional-memory-via-scalable-lookup and the 0.082-nat figure in over-tokenized-transformer-vocabulary-is-generally-worth-scaling; the 3.5% restart floor is in a-hitchhikers-guide-to-scaling-law-estimation (already cited).
suggested_fix: Swap the citation: replace [[moba-mixture-of-block-attention-for]] with [[conditional-memory-via-scalable-lookup]], [[over-tokenized-transformer-vocabulary-is-generally-worth-scaling]]; keep [[a-hitchhikers-guide-to-scaling-law-estimation]] for the 3.5% floor.

sentence: published architecture effects are 0.014–0.082 nats against a 3.5%-relative single-run floor
problem: The note supports the 3.5%-relative floor ('reported variance across random restarts ... reaches up to 3.5%') but contains no 0.014 or 0.082 nat figures; the effect-size range comes from the Engram and OverEncoding notes.
suggested_fix: Keep this note for the floor and add [[conditional-memory-via-scalable-lookup]] and [[over-tokenized-transformer-vocabulary-is-generally-worth-scaling]] for the 0.014–0.082 range.

sentence: with the largest gain on code — −1.3 PPL at 2K and −2.0 at 8K on GitHub
problem: The 0.762/0.986 averages and the 8.410/9.172/8.079/9.065 values are exact, but the −1.3/−2.0 GitHub deltas are INTRADoc vs UNIChunk, not vs MIXChunk, which is the baseline the sentence names. Against MIXChunk the GitHub column goes 5.531 → 4.252 (−1.28) at 2K and 7.496 → 5.010 (−2.49) at 8K, so the 8K figure is materially wrong for the stated comparison.

sentence: produces functional divergence within 10–17% of changing the data seed
problem: The note says FP arithmetic is 'within ~17% of data seed and ~10% of initialization seed' — the 10% is relative to the init seed, not the data seed. The sentence collapses both into a 10–17% band against the data seed.
suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'within ~17% of changing the data seed (and ~10% of changing the initialization seed)'.
